title: How can I know I am saved?
paragraphs: Understanding Assurance of Salvation

One of the most vital questions for any Christian is, "How can I know I am saved?" The Bible addresses this issue with clarity, offering believers a firm foundation for assurance. The nature of salvation, its evidence, and the promises of God all contribute to a confident faith in Christ.
The Basis of Salvation: Faith in Jesus Christ

The Scriptures teach that salvation is not earned by human effort or good works, but is a gift from God received through faith in Jesus Christ. This foundational truth is underscored throughout the New Testament:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV
He that believeth on the Son hath eternal life; but he that obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him. - John 3:36 ASV
The assurance of salvation rests not on our feelings, but on the objective promises of God's Word.
The Testimony of Scripture
God's Word offers clear assurance to those who have trusted Christ:
These things have I written unto you, that ye may know that ye have eternal life, even unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God. - 1 John 5:13 ASV
Notice the certainty: "that ye may know." Our assurance is grounded in believing God's testimony about His Son.
The Inner Witness of the Holy Spirit
Another aspect of assurance is the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit in the life of the believer:
The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are children of God. - Romans 8:16 ASV
While feelings can fluctuate, the Spirit’s witness aligns with God’s Word, assuring us of our relationship with Him.
Marks of Genuine Faith
While salvation is by faith alone, the Bible also teaches that genuine faith produces fruit. These are not the basis of salvation, but evidence of a transformed life:
Love for God and others (1 John 4:7 ASV)
Desire to obey God’s commands (1 John 2:3 ASV)
Repentance from sin (1 John 1:9 ASV)
Perseverance in faith (Philippians 1:6 ASV)
These evidences, while not perfect, demonstrate the ongoing work of God in a believer’s life.
Dealing with Doubt
Even sincere believers may sometimes struggle with doubts about their salvation. The solution is to return to God’s promises, not our performance or emotions:
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth him that sent me, hath eternal life, and cometh not into judgment, but hath passed out of death into life. - John 5:24 ASV
Assurance grows as we fix our eyes on Christ, trust His Word, and walk in fellowship with Him.
Summary

You can know you are saved if you have repented of your sin, trusted in Jesus Christ alone for salvation, and are resting in the promises of God’s Word. The Spirit confirms this, and your life will show evidence of His transforming grace. Assurance is not presumption, but faith in God’s unchanging truth.
